title: Automated control evidence conductor for residency & retention controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers and auditors frequently request proof that data residency and retention controls are enforced and evidence is available for SOC 2/ISO 27001 audits. Current evidence collection is manual or semi-automated across multiple systems (S3 buckets, KMS logs, VPC flow logs, Console configuration snapshots). This causes delays in SOC 2 readiness and increases engineering time for ad-hoc requests.

Goal: Build an "evidence conductor" that orchestrates collectors, normalizes artifacts, and generates audit-ready bundles mapped to control statements (SOC 2 CC, ISO 27001 controls) for residency and retention. The conductor should support scheduled and on-demand runs, a queryable evidence index, and API endpoints for exports to auditor tooling. It should integrate with existing collectors (Audit Harvester, Residency Mapper) and new lightweight connectors for Console snapshots, KMS export, and Dedicated capacity manifests.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor can run scheduled evidence collection for a customer and produce a signed artifact bundle (JSON + manifest) that maps to SOC 2/ISO 27001 control IDs.
Artifacts include provenance metadata (collector id, timestamp, sha256) and are stored in the customer evidence bucket with retention policy metadata.
UI/Console: PM can request a proof bundle for a customer and download a zip containing artifacts and the control mapping report.
API: /v1/compliance/evidence?customer_id=... returns index of collected artifacts and control mapping; supports on-demand run with async job id.
Integrations: at least three collectors validated (S3-config snapshot, KMS key rotation log export, and Console route config snapshot).
Automated regression tests for control mapping logic covering common edge cases (multi-region resources, aliasing of key ids).
implementation_steps: Design: finalize evidence artifact schema and manifest format (fields: artifact_id, control_ids[], collector, ts, sha256, retention_policy, bucket_path). Link: Confluence doc /compliance/evidence-schema (WIP).
Collector onboarding: define adapter interface (pull/push modes) and build adapters for Console snapshots, KMS exports, and Dedicated manifests.
Orchestration: implement Conductor service (stateless API + job runner) to schedule and coordinate collectors per-customer with retry and backoff.
Normalization: implement artifact normalizer to add provenance and map artifacts to control statements using the control registry (mapping table stored in repo).
Storage: write bundle and manifest to customer evidence bucket path `s3://redwood-evidence/<customer_id>/YYYY-MM-DD/<job_id>/` with server-side encryption and lifecycle tags.
UI/API: add Console page to request/download proofs and API endpoint for auditors. Add telemetry for job success/failure and artifact counts.
Tests & audits: end-to-end run against a staging customer, capture artifacts, and run sample auditor checklist to validate completeness.
Rollout: beta with 5 pilot customers, collect feedback, iterate on mapping gaps, then GA to all customers with Private/Dedicated tiers first.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Sensitive data may be accidentally included in artifacts (PII, secrets). Mitigation: artifact normalizer redacts known secrets and we provide a dry-run reviewer step before export; enforce denylists and redaction rules.
Risk: Mapping errors could misrepresent evidence coverage. Mitigation: keep mapping table in repo with schema versioning and automated unit tests; provide manual override annotations in Conductor UI.

Risk: Collector failures for on-prem customers (air-gapped). Mitigation: support an offline collector package that runs on customer infra and pushes signed bundles to the customer's evidence bucket or via secure transfer.
Risk: Large bundles and S3 egress costs. Mitigation: artifact deduplication and manifest-only exports for auditor previews; configure retention policies per customer tier.
